Say who gets one of two cookies: "One for Alice, one for me.", or "you" when no name is given.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/two-fer) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: two_fer.nomi
/// Says who gets the cookie: "One for Alice, one for me."
pub fn two_fer(name: String = "you") -> String {
    "One for ${name}, one for me."
}

// FILE: two_fer_test.nomi
import two_fer.two_fer

test "no name given" {
    assert two_fer() == "One for you, one for me."
}

test "a name given" {
    assert two_fer("Alice") == "One for Alice, one for me."
}

test "another name given" {
    assert two_fer("Bob") == "One for Bob, one for me."
}
```

## How it's written

- The missing name is a parameter default, `name: String = "you"`, rather than
  a `Maybe<String>`. The canonical `null` means "called without a name", and a
  default says that at the call site: `two_fer()`.
- Three plain `test` blocks rather than a `subtests` table: the first case
  calls with no argument, so the rows do not share a shape.
